"There in the dwelling of the moon"—the course [gātuḥ] has been explained. / "May they make a path for the people of the dawn"—there is also this Vedic quotation. / Daṃsayaḥ means deeds; they display [daṃsayanti] them. / "And to Kutsa in thought and deeds"—there is also this Vedic quotation. / "He has prospered; distress does not reach him." / He has prospered; distress does not reach him. Aṃhatiḥ, aṃhaḥ, and aṃhuḥ are from [the root] han- ("to strike"), with the penult removed and inverted. / "O Bṛhaspati, you chase away the malicious one." / O Bṛhaspati, because you drive away the hater of the gods. Pīyati is a verb of harming. Dyāvāpṛthivī ("Heaven and Earth") are separated [viyute], from being kept apart [viyavana]. / "Equal, separated, with distant ends." / "Equal" means having a common measure; mātrā ("measure") is from mā- ("to measure"). "Distant" has been explained. "End" [antaḥ] is that which is extended [ātataḥ]. Ṛdhak is an expression of being separate. And it is also seen in the sense of prospering [ṛdhnoti]: / "Prospering, you have sacrificed; and prospering, you have quieted [the victim]." / That is, "Prospering, you have sacrificed, and prospering, you have quieted." The forms asyāḥ and asya are accented with the acute on the first reference; they are unaccented on anaphoric reference. The acute has a stronger meaning; the unaccented has a weaker meaning: / "Be [favorable] unto us, for our acquisition, O goat-horsed one, not being angry, granting [wealth], / to those desiring fame, O goat-horsed one." / Be [favorable] unto us for our acquisition; not being angry means not raging; granting [rarivān], from rā- ("to give"), reduplicated. By "goat-horsed" [ajāśva] he addresses Pūṣan; ajāśva means having goats as horses, or born from non-goats. / Now the unaccented: / "Long-lived may her husband live for a hundred autumns." / Long-lived may her husband live for a hundred autumns. Autumn [śarad] is when crops are ripened [śṛtāḥ] in it, or because waters are diminished [śīrṇāḥ]. / Asya is explained by this [explanation of] asyāḥ.

4.s: asya vāmasya palitasya hotus tasya bhrātā madhyamo asty aśnah | tṛtīyo bhrātā ghṛtapṛṣṭho asyātrāpaśyam viśpatim saptaputram | asya vāmasya vananīyasya palitasya pālayituḥ hotuḥ hvātavyasya tasya bhrātā madhyamo asty aśanah | bhrātā bharater harati karmaṇo harate bhāgam bhartavyo bhavati iti vā | tṛtīyo bhrātā ghṛta pṛṣṭho asya ayam agnih | tatra apaśyam sarvasya pātāram vā pālayitāram vā viśpatim sapta putram saptama putram saparṇa putram iti vā | sapta sṛptā saṅkhyā sapta āditya raśmayaḥ iti vadanti ||
4.d: अस्य वामस्य पलितस्य होतुस् तस्य भ्राता मध्यमो अस्त्य् अश्नह् । तृतीयो भ्राता घृतपृष्ठो अस्यात्रापश्यम् विश्पतिम् सप्तपुत्रम् । अस्य वामस्य वननीयस्य पलितस्य पालयितुः होतुः ह्वातव्यस्य तस्य भ्राता मध्यमो अस्त्य् अशनह् । भ्राता भरतेर् हरति कर्मणो हरते भागम् भर्तव्यो भवति इति वा । तृतीयो भ्राता घृत पृष्ठो अस्य अयम् अग्निह् । तत्र अपश्यम् सर्वस्य पातारम् वा पालयितारम् वा विश्पतिम् सप्त पुत्रम् सप्तम पुत्रम् सपर्ण पुत्रम् इति वा । सप्त सृप्ता सङ्ख्या सप्त आदित्य रश्मयः इति वदन्ति ॥
4.m: "Of this beloved, gray-haired priest, his middle brother is the devouring [wind]; / his third brother has ghee on his back; here I saw the lord of the clan with seven sons." / Of this "beloved" [vāmasya], that is, desirable; "gray-haired" [palitasya], that is, protector; / "priest" [hotuḥ], that is, one to be invoked; "his middle brother is the devouring [wind]" [aśanaḥ]. "Brother" [bhrātā] is from bhṛ- ("to bear"), meaning to carry [harati]; he carries off his share, or he is one to be supported [bhartavyaḥ]. "His third brother has ghee on his back": this is Agni. "There I saw the protector or guardian of all, / the lord of the clan with seven sons"—either the seventh son or having moving [sarpaṇa] sons. / Seven [sapta] is a number that is reached [sṛptā]; they say [they are] the seven rays of the sun.

4.s: sapta yuñjanti ratham eka cakram eko aśvo vahati saptanāmā | trinābhi cakram ajaram anarvam yatremā viśvā bhuvanādhi tasthuh | sapta yuñjanti ratham eka cakram eka cārinam | cakraṃś cakater vā carater vā krāmater vā | eko aśvo vahati sapta nāmā ādityah, sapta asmai raśmayo rasān abhisamnāmayanti, sapta enam ṛṣayaḥ stuvanti iti vā | idam api itarat nāma etasmād eva abhisamnāmāt | saṃvatsara pradhāna uttaro ardharcah | tri nābhi cakram tri ṛtuḥ saṃvatsaro grīsmo varṣā hemanta iti | saṃvatsaraḥ saṃvasante'asmin bhūtāni | grīsmo grasyante'asmin rasā, varṣā varṣaty āsu parjanyas, hemanto himavān, himam punar hanter vā nihoter vā | ajaram ajarana dharmānam anarvam apratyṛtam anyasmin | yatra imāni sarvāṇi bhūtāny abhisaṃtiṣṭhante tam saṃvatsaram sarva mātrābhiḥ stauti | pañcāre cakre parivartamāne iti pañca ṛtutayā | pañca ṛtavaḥ saṃvatsarasya iti ca brāhmaṇam hemanta śiśirayoḥ samāsena | saḷara āhur arpitam iti sas ṛtutayā | arāḥ pratyṛtā nābhau | sas punaḥ sahateh | dvādaśāram nahi tajjarāya | dvādaśa pradhayaś cakramekam | iti māsānām | māsā mānāt | pradhiḥ prahito bhavati | etasmint sākam triśatā na śaṅkavor pitāḥ sastir na calācalāsah | sastiś ca ha vai trīni ca śatāni saṃvatsarasya ahorātrā iti ca brāhmaṇam samāsena | sapta śatāni viṃśatiś ca tasthuh | sapta ca vai śatāni viṃśatiś ca saṃvatsarasya ahorātrā iti ca brāhmaṇam vibhāgena vibhāgena ||
4.d: सप्त युञ्जन्ति रथम् एक चक्रम् एको अश्वो वहति सप्तनामा । त्रिनाभि चक्रम् अजरम् अनर्वम् यत्रेमा विश्वा भुवनाधि तस्थुह् । सप्त युञ्जन्ति रथम् एक चक्रम् एक चारिनम् । चक्रंश् चकतेर् वा चरतेर् वा क्रामतेर् वा । एको अश्वो वहति सप्त नामा आदित्यह्, सप्त अस्मै रश्मयो रसान् अभिसम्नामयन्ति, सप्त एनम् ऋषयः स्तुवन्ति इति वा । इदम् अपि इतरत् नाम एतस्माद् एव अभिसम्नामात् । संवत्सर प्रधान उत्तरो अर्धर्चह् । त्रि नाभि चक्रम् त्रि ऋतुः संवत्सरो ग्रीस्मो वर्षा हेमन्त इति । संवत्सरः संवसन्तेऽअस्मिन् भूतानि । ग्रीस्मो ग्रस्यन्तेऽअस्मिन् रसा, वर्षा वर्षत्य् आसु पर्जन्यस्, हेमन्तो हिमवान्, हिमम् पुनर् हन्तेर् वा निहोतेर् वा । अजरम् अजरन धर्मानम् अनर्वम् अप्रत्यृतम् अन्यस्मिन् । यत्र इमानि सर्वाणि भूतान्य् अभिसंतिष्ठन्ते तम् संवत्सरम् सर्व मात्राभिः स्तौति । पञ्चारे चक्रे परिवर्तमाने इति पञ्च ऋतुतया । पञ्च ऋतवः संवत्सरस्य इति च ब्राह्मणम् हेमन्त शिशिरयोः समासेन । सऌअर आहुर् अर्पितम् इति सस् ऋतुतया । अराः प्रत्यृता नाभौ । सस् पुनः सहतेह् । द्वादशारम् नहि तज्जराय । द्वादश प्रधयश् चक्रमेकम् । इति मासानाम् । मासा मानात् । प्रधिः प्रहितो भवति । एतस्मिन्त् साकम् त्रिशता न शङ्कवोर् पिताः सस्तिर् न चलाचलासह् । सस्तिश् च ह वै त्रीनि च शतानि संवत्सरस्य अहोरात्रा इति च ब्राह्मणम् समासेन । सप्त शतानि विंशतिश् च तस्थुह् । सप्त च वै शतानि विंशतिश् च संवत्सरस्य अहोरात्रा इति च ब्राह्मणम् विभागेन विभागेन ॥
4.m: "Seven yoke the chariot with one wheel; one horse with seven names draws it; / the three-naved wheel is ageless, unarrested, wherein all these worlds abide." / Seven yoke the chariot; "with one wheel" means moving alone; cakra ("wheel") is from cak- ("to resist"), or from car- ("to move"), or from kram- ("to step"). One horse with seven names draws it: [this is] the sun; seven rays bend [sannāmayanti] the juices toward him; or seven sages praise him. This other name [of the horse] is also from this very [root], from bending toward [abhisannāma]. The latter half-verse has the year as its main subject: "the three-naved wheel"; the year has three seasons: summer, rains, and winter. The year [saṃvatsara] is that in which beings dwell together [saṃvasante]. In summer [grīṣma] the juices are devoured [grasyante]. In the rainy season [varṣā] Parjanya rains [varṣati] upon them. Winter [hemanta] has snow [hima]; hima in turn is from han- ("to strike") or from hi- ("to send"). "Ageless" [ajaram] means having the property of not aging. "Unarrested" [anarvam] means not fitted into another. Wherein all these beings abide—that year he praises in all its measures: / "In the wheel with five spokes turning round"— / thus with five seasons; and there is the Brāhmaṇa: "The year has five seasons," by combining winter and the cool season. / "They say it is fixed on six spokes"— / thus with six seasons. Spokes [arāḥ] are fitted into the nave [nābhi]; six [ṣaṭ] in turn is from sah- ("to overcome"). / "Having twelve spokes, it is indeed not for decay; / twelve are the fellies, the wheel is one"— / thus of the months; months [māsāḥ] are from mā- ("to measure"); a felly [pradhiḥ] is set forward [prahitaḥ]. / "In it three hundred and sixty pegs are fitted together, not loose." / "Three hundred and sixty are indeed the days and nights of the year," / says the Brāhmaṇa by combining them. / "Seven hundred and twenty stood"— / "Seven hundred and twenty are indeed the days and nights of the year," / says the Brāhmaṇa by distinguishing them, by distinguishing them.
